> A Simple Midi keyboard that play's many instruments and has a custom edited software. It has 3 switches, one rotary encoder, 2 slider pots, a capacitive touchboard and a rotary potentiometer all powered with a waveshare esp32 s3 zero mini

### 2026-10-23 – # # What I did in this session

**1.85h**

# # What I did in this session
### ~ So I Started working on the schematic and completed it. The Process was pretty straightforward as this time i knew my way around the software, however i did get stuck sometimes like when finding the sliders and putting values, but it was overall easy.
---
## I also did NOT follow the GUIDE 1:1, i added a ROTARY POT (potentiometer) to the midi board and i will also be changing its software as well.

## It took me like 20 mins to decide what footprint to use for the rotary potentiometer so after searching for it, i eventually decided to use _"Potentiometer_THT:Potentiometer_Alps_RK163___Single___Horizontal"

---
## Overall it was very easy this time but it still took  me like almost (touching) 2 hours to complete all of this.
---

# # What i did
## ~ I completed the making of capacitive touch buttons and lemme clear one thing, IT TOOK ME LIKE 40MINS STRAIGHT UP, and then i also made the pcb outline and now all that is left is routing and then 3d models adding, rendering and software, and i'm going to do that after this.
---
## The other stuff such as footprint of rotary potentiometer also took me a lot of time as i didn't know how to place and use it if it's horizontally laid down, so i just placed it at the end of the board and it kinda hangs off the board so i can use it properly.
---
## I also had to resize and remake the capacitive buttons as i had made them too small and they were the size of an fingernail each 😭. SO it took me more time than expected
---

# Routed the pcb
